record.paper_title: Open problems on structure of positively curved projective varieties
record.context_brief: Truly flat tangent vectors and fibrations
record.original_question: Let (X,g) be a compact Kähler manifold with semi-positive or semi-negative holomorphic sectional curvature. Let V be the set of appropriate truly flat tangent vectors, where a truly flat tangent vector v at p satisfies R_g(v,x,y,z̄)=0 for all x,y,z in T_X,p. Does V determine an integrable subbundle of T_X, and can one find a complementary subbundle W with T_X ≅ W ⊕ V? In the semi-positive case, can this splitting construct an MRC fibration f: X → Y with W equal to the relative tangent bundle T_{X/Y}; in the semi-negative case, can it construct the Iitaka fibration f: X → Z associated with K_X with V equal to T_{X/Z}?

evidence.quote: Here a tangent vector v ∈ TX,p at a point p ∈ X is said to be truly flat if it satisfies that Rg(v, x, y, z̄) = 0 for any x, y, z ∈ TX,p.
Problem 3.7. — Let (X, g) be a compact Kähler manifold with semi-positive (or semi-negative) holomorphic sectional curvature. Let V ⊂ TX be the set of “appropriate” truly flat tangent vectors.
Does V determine an integrable subbundle of TX?
Can we find a subbundle W ⊂ TX such that TX ∼= W ⊕ V ?
In the case of semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvatures, can we construct an MRC fibration f : X → Y such that W = TX/Y ?
In the case of semi-negative holomorphic sectional curvatures, can we construct the Iitaka fibration f : X → Z associated with the canonical bundle KX such that V = TX/Z?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,g)$ be a compact Kähler manifold, and let $R_g$ denote its Chern curvature tensor. Say that a tangent vector $v \in T_{X,p}$ at a point $p \in X$ is truly flat if
$$R_g(v,x,y,\bar z) = 0 \quad \text{for all } x,y,z \in T_{X,p}.$$
Assume that $(X,g)$ has either semi-positive or semi-negative holomorphic sectional curvature, and let $V \subset T_X$ be the (appropriately chosen) subset of truly flat tangent vectors.

(a) Does $V$ define an integrable holomorphic subbundle of $T_X$?

(b) Does there exist a holomorphic subbundle $W \subset T_X$ such that $T_X \cong W \oplus V$?

(c) In the semi-positive case, does this splitting produce a maximally rationally connected (MRC) fibration $f \colon X \to Y$ onto a smooth projective variety $Y$ with $W = T_{X/Y}$?

(d) In the semi-negative case, does this splitting produce the Iitaka fibration $f \colon X \to Z$ associated to the canonical bundle $K_X$ with $V = T_{X/Z}$?
artifact.category_tag: Kähler manifolds with semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results are known. In the semi-positive case, when truly flat vectors vanish (e.g. quasi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature), the manifold is projective and rationally connected, and recent works (Matsumura and others) show that MRC fibrations of such manifolds can be made into smooth morphisms onto manifolds whose canonical bundle is not big, with the tangent subsheaf forming an integrable subbundle in various cases. A complete answer establishing the integrable splitting $T_X \cong W \oplus V$ and the identification with the MRC/Iitaka fibration in full generality does not appear to be available in the literature.

status_evidence.title: On the image of MRC fibrations of projective manifolds with semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature
status_evidence.snippet: Conjectures on structures and images of MRC fibrations of smooth projective varieties admitting semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature; proves canonical bundle of image is not big.
status_evidence.claim: Partial structural results on MRC fibrations under semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature.

status_evidence.title: Positivity of tangent sheaves of projective varieties — structure of MRC fibrations
status_evidence.snippet: Subsheaf of tangent vectors forms a subbundle of the tangent bundle and determines an integrable foliation.
status_evidence.claim: Integrability part of the problem has been addressed in specific settings.

status_evidence.title: On projective manifolds with semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature
status_evidence.snippet: Pseudo-effective holonomy principle: if no nonzero truly flat tangent vector exists, the manifold is projective and rationally connected.
status_evidence.claim: Truly flat vectors govern rational connectedness, supporting the conjectural picture.
